site.name: Amzy
site.location: Arkansas Mountain / south of Fourmile Creek
overview: Amzy was a documented Boulder County tungsten prospect on the north slope of Arkansas Mountain, south of Fourmile Creek.
Colorado's statewide tungsten inventory records a short adit, no recorded production, and a large vein of hard ore at the property.

timeline.text: Boulder County land-management research records the Amzy lode survey date as October 29, 1932.
Colorado's statewide tungsten inventory listed Amzy as owned by Skydale, Inc., with no recorded production and a short adit; Doc Hill was identified as the last operator.

moreHistory: The state tungsten inventory places Amzy in Section 20, T1N R71W on the north slope of Arkansas Mountain south of Fourmile Creek. It describes a short adit and a large vein of hard ore, but records no production.

A matching Amzy / Great Sphinx occurrence is retained in Gold Hill Mining District locality records near 40.03722, -105.36750. The coordinate is used as a historic site-level identification point and does not imply that the adit is open or that a surviving portal has been field-surveyed.
Boulder County's Betasso Preserve management history independently documents portions of the Amzy lode within the Benjamin property and records historic mining features in that landscape.
